1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorizedMfa(), which requires a valid server-side session whose accountId matches the account, and no client-supplied account identifier is ever accepted.

2.why: Verification codes are hashed and bound to a specific pendingIdentities entry keyed by a random preauth cookie and accountId, with used/expiry checks, so a code is not usable by any other user.

3.why: verify-enrollment enables MFA without invalidating or rotating the existing session; sessions are only deleted on logout, so the pre-MFA session continues to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encryptAtRest) and recovery codes are stored as argon2id hashes via Bun.password.hash.

5.why: All secrets, codes, tokens, and the encryption key are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: Cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, and the CSRF token and recovery codes live only in in-memory JS state.

7.why: Server-side validators (isValidEmail, isValidPhone, isOtp, isRecovery) plus strict JSON body typing validate all user input before use.

8.why: The UI builds DOM exclusively with textContent/createTextNode (no innerHTML) and responses carry a nonce-based CSP, preventing injected markup from executing.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all (only JSON/HTML responses on same-origin routes), so no open redirect exists.

10.why: headersFor sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie and pendingCookie both set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: The server logs nothing sensitive, uses no secret-bearing URLs, and returns only generic errors, but the mock client intentionally writes OTPs and recovery codes to the browser console/Logs panel as simulated delivery.

13.why: Sign-in codes and provisioning challenges carry used flags and 5-minute expiries and are deleted after use; TOTP is 30-second time-bound and recovery codes are removed upon consumption.

14.why: Sign-in, identity verification, enrollment OTP, and recovery-code paths all implement attempt counters with a 5-attempt/10-minute lockout policy.

15.why: A fresh random SID is issued at verify-identity (rotation on authentication), sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
